audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty prose never states WHY the early lane is hard: Mel throws Radiant Volley at 950 and Solar Snare at 1000, while Azir must stand at 525 to place a Sand Soldier. The page called the lane 'Skill' for levels 1-5 while the packet levelChart and the content win[] rows both say Mel.
audit.why: Range asymmetry from both kits: Mel Q 950, Mel E 1000, Azir W 525 (soldier placement). Azir's only escape, Shifting Sands, is 22s at rank 1 against an 11s root.
audit.corrected: Early is Mel's; the lane flips at Nashor's. Level chart moved to Mel for rows 0-3 with the whys rewritten to match, and Level 6 set to Azir to agree with the content layer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were generic ('poke becomes deletion') and never named Mel's own spikes: Golden Eclipse at 6 (120/100/80s, global, scales with Overwhelm stacks) and Rebuttal's falling cooldown (38s at rank 1 down to 26s).
audit.why: Azir's spike is Nashor's Tooth (soldier autos become sustained damage that a single 38s barrier cannot blank). Mel's spike is level 6, where accumulated Overwhelm becomes a map-wide execute.
audit.corrected: spikes[0..3].text and breakdown.spikes rewritten around Solar Snare's 11s root, Golden Eclipse's global Overwhelm scaling, Nashor's, and Emperor's Divide vs a dashless Mel.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly claimed Rebuttal 'reflects your projectiles back' as the whole story and used it as a burst-damage warning. Riot's text says Rebuttal ALSO prevents her from taking damage outright — that is the decisive interaction for Azir, because a soldier volley into it is zeroed regardless of whether soldier attacks count as projectiles. Nothing on the page named Solar Snare, Radiant Volley, Searing Brilliance or Golden Eclipse (packet defect confirmed).
audit.why: Enemy kit W: 'forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage, and grants her movement speed', 38/35/33/29/26s. Enemy kit E Solar Snare: 1000 range root, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s — a root denies Azir's Shifting Sands dash (22/20.5/19/17.5/16s), so her root returns twice per dash Azir spends. Passive Searing Brilliance is an auto-attack reset that loads 3 bonus projectiles per ability cast (up to 9) — the wind-up, not the cast, is the tell. Golden Eclipse (120/100/80s) hits every Overwhelm-stacked target at any distance.
audit.corrected: All five Mel ability names now appear; Rebuttal described as damage prevention on a real cooldown; Solar Snare vs Shifting Sands stated as the root-beats-dash interaction; Golden Eclipse tied to Overwhelm stacking and recall discipline; Emperor's Divide framed as a wall a dashless Mel cannot cross.

audit.why: 54.43% over 384 games, consistent with a scaling-favoured lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (known defect class).
audit.why: Rebuttal 38s at rank 1; Solar Snare 11s; Shifting Sands 22s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with all three numbers and the dash-vs-root ratio.

audit.whatIsWrong: Searing Brilliance's auto-attack reset was never mentioned as the burst tell.
audit.why: Passive loads bonus projectiles onto her NEXT attack after any ability cast, so the attack wind-up follows the ability.
audit.corrected: Folded into dosFull[0] and the early-game text as a step-back cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mel was called 'he/his/him' across tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, loading, breakdown.wave, dosFull and dontsFull titles.
audit.corrected: All pronouns corrected in the proposed strings.

edits.before: Mel's kit punishes aggressive trading thanks to her reflect passive, so avoid throwing needless poke into her and instead focus on safe soldier farming from max range. She out-trades you in raw poke damage in this window, so respect her cooldowns and don't overextend for CS. Ward tri-bush since she can set up poke angles you won't see coming otherwise.
edits.after: Rebuttal is a barrier, not a passive: while it is up she takes no damage, so a volley into it is wasted mana — bait it and count 38 seconds. Radiant Volley reaches 950 and you must stand at 525 to place sand, so farm through soldiers and accept the chip. Her attack wind-up after any cast is the burst tell, not the cast. Ward river; Solar Snare roots at 1000.

edits.before: At 6 her ultimate threatens to execute you if she's built a damage lead, but this is also when your own R comes online, giving you a real tool to disengage or wall off her line of sight. Play for wave management and side-lane pressure with soldiers rather than direct duels in this stretch. If you can avoid dying to her level 6 spike, your scaling starts to take over quickly after.
edits.after: Golden Eclipse is global and its damage scales with the Overwhelm stacks she has already put on you, so a chipped health bar is a kill anywhere on the map — recall earlier than feels necessary. Emperor's Divide arrives at the same level and is your answer to Solar Snare: wall behind her when she steps up and she has no dash to get back. Play waves and soldier pressure, not duels.

edits.before: Your first item brings your poke and clear to a level that starts overwhelming her more limited kit, and by two items your zone control with R and soldiers is simply superior to anything she brings to a teamfight. Build MR if she's ahead on kills (Abyssal Mask), since her burst execute remains a threat into squishies. In fights, use soldiers to control space and hold R to block her engage or peel for your team.
edits.after: Nashor's Tooth turns soldier autos into sustained damage, and one 38-second Rebuttal only blanks a slice of it. By two items Emperor's Divide decides fights: Mel carries no dash, so a wall behind her cuts her off from her team completely. Build MR if she is ahead (Abyssal Mask) — Golden Eclipse still reaches your health bar from anywhere on the map. Hold R for her step-up, not for the opening.

edits.before: Avoid feeding her passive reflect damage in early trades
edits.after: Avoid spending soldier volleys into her Rebuttal barrier
